title: Give the brain a sense
summary: Add an input of your own, then use what the SUV senses to shape its habits.

steps.title: A sense of your own
steps.body:
The brain only knows its inputs: lidar beams, the lane, the route, the light, the car ahead, people and its speed. A `sensor` line adds one more input, after the built in ones.

Give it a name, a label, a range and a value. Brains work best with inputs between 0 and 1, so the range tells the app how to squeeze the value. Add a sensor for how many seconds behind the car ahead the SUV is, from 0 s to 10 s. A sensor changes the shape of the brain, so a run already training starts a new branch.

check.message: The brain should have 26 inputs: the standard 25 and your sensor.

hints: The pattern is sensor name "Label" in low .. high = value.
Write sensor gapTime "Seconds behind the car ahead" in 0 s .. 10 s = min(carAhead.gap / max(car.speed, 1 m/s), 10 s).

steps.title: Keep your distance
steps.body:
Sensors are also there for rewards. `lidar.min` is the shortest lidar beam, the distance to whatever is closest: a curb, a building, a car or a person.

A crash ends the trip, but it comes too late to teach much. A small cost for coming within 1.5 m of anything teaches brains to keep clear before it happens.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses lidar.min.

hints: Write a cost that applies when lidar.min is small.

steps.title: A safe gap
steps.body:
Other cars drive from level 4 on. `carAhead.seen` is true while a car is ahead in the lane, and `carAhead.gap` is the bumper to bumper gap.

A safe gap grows with speed. Multiplying a time by `car.speed` turns it into meters, so `1.5 s * car.speed` is the distance the SUV covers in a second and a half.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses carAhead.gap.

hints: Only charge it while a car is ahead: carAhead.seen and something about the gap.
Write reward -0.01 when carAhead.seen and carAhead.gap < 1.5 s * car.speed.
